actual_scope: Prove, for the 104 ports of P104 and the 120 ports of full E8 (P120), that: no subspace of dimension >= 5 is saturated (all odd vectors ports), with exact counts of saturated subspaces of dimension 1..4; the maximum number of ports in a subspace of dimension e is 1, 2, 4, 8, 12, 20, 36 for e = 1..7 for both sets; the maximum of N(V)N(V^perp) is the port degree (48 on P104 at every dimension; 56 or 48 on P120); and the best flag rectangle has mass 32 at every level except 36 at level 5, with P104 at 30 on the two end levels.
scope_change_reason: The card asks for a helper-basis and causal-split construction on the complete invoice. This package is a statement about port sets only: it constructs no word, prices nothing and splits nothing. It fixes the sharing geometry (subspace counts, bicliques and flag rectangles) that any later construction on these ports is bounded by.
bottleneck_link: docs/research/research-family-status.md; the statements bound how much one carrier can share on the E8 orthogonality graph at each level, for P104 and for full E8.
stop_rule: No kappa claim. The statements are about the port set alone; Theorem 1 is proved by hand and re-counted, Theorems 2-4 are exact exhaustive results without a closed-form proof. No word is constructed and nothing is priced.
evidence: README.md (statements, proof of saturation depth, description of the exhaustive enumeration), check.py (exact recomputation from the port list and from coordinates for P120).

open_questions.question: Is there a closed-form derivation of N_e = 2^(e-2) + 4 for 4 <= e <= 7 and of the flag masses, from the radical of V and the restriction of q to V?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It would turn the exhaustive tables into theorems valid for any E8-type port set and show why the bias 4 stops growing and the pattern fails at e = 8.
open_questions.first_step: For a subspace V of dimension e, write N(V) as half the odd vectors plus a bias given by the radical dimension of B restricted to V and the value of q on it, then check the formula against the enumerated maxima for e = 4..7.
open_questions.blocked_by: Only a sketch of the radical argument exists; the bias term has not been derived and the e = 8 case (64 and 60) does not fit it.

open_questions.question: Can the lower bounds of 52 (P104) and 60 (P120) on covering the edges of the dot-0 graph by subspace bicliques be raised or attained?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The star law says no single subspace biclique beats one star; the covering number says how many are needed, which measures how much sharing is possible at all.
open_questions.first_step: Enumerate the maximal subspace bicliques ports(V) x ports(V^perp) for one dimension e, then solve the fractional cover LP over them.
open_questions.blocked_by: Only the maximum mass per dimension is computed; the full list of maximal bicliques for e = 3..6 has not been enumerated.

open_questions.question: Which punctures of P120 (removing two disjoint orthoframes of eight lines) keep N_e for e <= 7 and the star-law values, and is P104 typical among them?
open_questions.why_it_matters: If every such puncture keeps them, the invariants say nothing about the particular choice of puncture; if only a few do, the choice is a structural fact about P104.
open_questions.first_step: List the orthoframes inside P120 (8-cliques of port-dot-1 lines), pick several disjoint pairs, and rerun the exhaustive pass of check.py with the removed set changed.
open_questions.blocked_by: The orthoframes of P120 have not been enumerated or classified under the symmetry group of E8.
